newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo head appeals bribery conviction.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo head appeals bribery conviction.

text.p: Daewoo Group Chairman Kim Woo-choong has appealed to the Supreme Court against his conviction for bribing former president Roh Tae-woo, a group official said on Monday.
The official at Daewoo's legal affairs division, who declined to be named, said the appeal was lodged on Saturday.
"The sentence is not a problem. What matters is that a conviction will bring various restrictions on the chairman's activities," the official said.
Last week an appeals court suspended Kim's two-year jail sentence for three years. He was convicted of offering bribes to Roh during Roh's tenure in office from 1988-93.
The same appeals court cut Roh's sentence to 17 years from 22-1/2 years on charges of corruption as well as mutiny and treason over a 1979 coup and 1980 army massacre.
